stages.name: Satisficing vs profit maximisation: weighing the objectives
stages.title: Satisficing vs profit maximisation: weighing the objectives
stages.sub: After this stage the student can evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of satisficing against profit maximisation.

steps.q: A firm's managers, workers and shareholders all want different things from the business. If it chases only one goal, such as maximum profit, do the other groups' demands get met?
steps.right: No, their demands are pushed aside
steps.wrong: Yes, one goal covers everyone's demands
steps.hint: Think about whether one target can satisfy groups who each want something different.

steps.q: Now suppose the firm instead aims for 'good enough' across several goals at once. Does any one stakeholder group get completely ignored?
steps.right: No, each gets some reasonable attention
steps.wrong: Yes, one group is still ignored completely
steps.hint: Spreading attention across several goals rather than one: what happens to each group's share?

steps.q: Real managers rarely have perfect information or unlimited time to calculate the exact profit-maximising output. Given these limits on their decision-making, could they realistically hit the exact maximising point every time?
steps.wrong: Yes, they could still hit it exactly
steps.hint: Think about what limits a manager's information, time and ability to calculate.

steps.q: The MC=MR rule shows the exact output where profit is highest. A firm using satisficing stops adjusting output once profit feels 'good enough', short of that point. Is its output now at the level MC=MR points to, or below it?
steps.right: Below the level MC=MR points to
steps.wrong: Still at the level MC=MR points to
steps.hint: Has the firm carried on adjusting all the way to where MC=MR, or stopped earlier?

steps.q: Because output stays short of the MC=MR point, is the firm producing at the most efficient level, or missing out on some of it?
steps.wrong: Still at the most efficient level
steps.hint: If output falls short of the profit-maximising point, what happens to efficiency at that level?

steps.right: No, it comes down to personal opinion
steps.hint: Is 'good enough' a fixed figure like profit, or a judgement call?

steps.wrong: Yes, just as easily as checking profit

steps.q: A firm producing at the MC=MR output earns the highest profit possible this year, rather than stopping early. What does that maximum profit leave the firm holding onto, once costs and distributions are covered?
steps.right: A larger pool of retained earnings
steps.wrong: No more than a satisficing firm would keep
steps.hint: If profit is higher than under satisficing, what happens to the amount left over inside the firm?

steps.q: A recession hits and sales fall sharply. Does having a larger pool of retained earnings built up in good years help the firm survive the downturn?
steps.right: Yes, it gives a cushion to survive
steps.wrong: No, it makes no difference to survival
steps.hint: Think about what a firm can draw on when revenue suddenly drops.
